about: A held-out check: worked examples from Social Security's operating manual (POMS) that were never scored in content/eval/ssa-examples.json and never used to change the rules engine, run once on the engine as frozen at the commit in held-out-results.json. Every passage is SSA's own text, read from the URL given. As in the main set, dates are moved to 2026 so 2026 and 2027 amounts apply and the facts are SSA's. Each gift card is entered the way Giftwise treats a gift card today, as cash (src/lib/channel3.ts), decided before the run.
encoding_rule: A gift card or gift certificate is entered as a cash gift of its face value, category other, because that is how Giftwise treats every gift card (src/lib/channel3.ts). The facts and the encoding of the gifts were not changed after the first run; two expected answers were, as recorded in corrections.

corrections.what: The first run expected the whole face value after the infrequent exclusion ($3,100 and $200). SSA's text says the value is income subject to the income exclusions, the convention of the main set (POMS SI 00810.410: the first $60 a quarter), so the expected values are $3,040 and $140.

The first run's scorer did not count the one-third reduction as income, the main set's reading of whether help adds anything. SSA counts the reduction as income, so the held-out scorer now does (src/lib/held-out.ts). Both check amounts matched in the first run.

cases.title: A $3,100 store gift card received as an award
cases.passage: Bernie Winters receives an award settlement in the form of an Xmart gift card worth $3100. (See Awards, SI 00830.515.) There is no restriction on the use of the gift card in Xmart stores, nor is there any legally enforceable prohibition on its resale. Treat the gift card at its face value as unearned income in the month it is received, subject to the rules pertaining to income and income exclusions for SSI purposes.
cases.situation: Bernie receives SSI and lives alone with no other income. In April 2026 Bernie receives a $3,100 Xmart gift card with no restriction on its use in Xmart stores and no prohibition on resale.
cases.ssa_answer: Income at its face value in the month it is received, subject to the income exclusions: $3,100 less the $60 infrequent or irregular income exclusion leaves $3,040.

cases.title: A $200 Visa gift card from a friend
cases.passage: Liza Garcia receives a $200 Visa gift card from a friend for use at any locations where Visa debit cards are accepted, including retail stores and online merchants. The gift card includes a prohibition against the beneficiary selling the card to another individual, applying the value as a payment to a store credit card account, or redeeming the card for cash. Thus, it is restricted on its use. However, it can be used to purchase food or shelter items. We treat the Visa gift card as unearned income based on its value ($200) in the month that it is received, subject to the rules pertaining to income and income exclusions for SSI purposes.
cases.situation: Liza receives SSI and lives alone with no other income. In May 2026 a friend gives her a $200 Visa gift card that cannot be resold but can buy food.
cases.ssa_answer: Income at its value in the month it is received, subject to the income exclusions: $200 less the $60 infrequent or irregular income exclusion leaves $140.

cases.title: A $100 office-supply gift certificate that cannot be resold
cases.passage: Edwin Blacksmith receives a $100 Office Warehouse gift certificate from a friend for use at any Office Warehouse store. The gift certificate is restricted for use to purchase only office supplies and has a legally enforceable prohibition on its resale. Since the beneficiary cannot use the gift certificate to purchase food or shelter, nor can the beneficiary sell the gift certificate for cash, do not count the gift certificate as income and it does not meet the definition of a resource.
cases.situation: Edwin receives SSI and lives alone with no other income. In June 2026 a friend gives him a $100 Office Warehouse gift certificate, usable only for office supplies and legally barred from resale.
cases.ssa_answer: Not income, and not a resource: it cannot buy food or shelter and cannot be sold.

cases.title: A $50 birthday gift card from a daughter
cases.passage: Phillip Evans receives a $50 birthday gift card from their daughter. Phillip did not receive any other income from their daughter during the calendar quarter. Therefore, exclude the gift card as infrequent or irregular income.
cases.situation: Phillip receives SSI and lives alone with no other income. In August 2026 his daughter gives him a $50 birthday gift card, the only income from her that quarter.
cases.ssa_answer: Excluded as infrequent or irregular income.

cases.title: The one-third reduction after a cost-of-living increase
cases.part: E, Example: Individual Subject To VTR Prior To FBR Increase
cases.passage: 1. Facts/Information a. Individual eligible since 1990. b. Individual subject to VTR since April 1992. c. CI: $0 d. Cost-of-Living Adjustment: effective January 2000 ... 3. Payment Computations a. January 2000 $512.00 - 0.00 -170.66 January FBR FCI in November 1999 VTR charged 11/99 - Value of VTR based on increased 2000 FBR due to COLA 341.34 January Payment
cases.situation: Kim receives SSI with no income and lives in her brother's household, which gives her food and shelter for nothing, so the one-third reduction applies. The cost-of-living increase takes effect in January 2027. Consider the checks paid in December 2026 and January 2027, set by October and November 2026.
cases.ssa_answer: The reduction for the January 2027 check is one third of the new year's rate, charged on November's support: $1,029 less $343 is $686 (SSA's own figures for 2000: $512 less $170.66 is $341.34). The December 2026 check stays at 2026 amounts: $994 less $331.33 is $662.67.

not_scored.what: Gift cards from FEMA after a declared disaster
not_scored.why: Disaster assistance from a government agency, not a gift from family or friends.

not_scored.what: Whether the one-third reduction applies to a living arrangement
not_scored.why: The living arrangement is an input Giftwise asks for, not something the engine decides.

not_scored.what: Cash from household members above their share of expenses
not_scored.why: Pro rata shares of a household's expenses, a separate calculation from a gift.
